goldens.comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.

With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `UsernameForm.authenticate()` now calling a no-arg `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()`, but the diff does not show the rest of `UsernameForm` or its superclasses. While the diff adds an `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel)` helper to `UsernamePasswordForm`, that does not prove a no-arg method is absent elsewhere. Therefore the claim that “only an overload taking UserModel exists” and that the module “does not compile” cannot be verified from the provided diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernamePasswordForm.java:161 — Condition `user != null` inverts the old `user == null` check, so passkey/conditional-UI data is no longer filled on normal first login (no user yet).

adjudication.rationale: In `UsernamePasswordForm.challenge(...)`, the old behavior explicitly called `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` when `context.getUser() == null` (initial/first-render case). The diff replaces this with `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, and `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns true only when `user != null`. That inverts the previous gate, so on a normal first login where no user is identified yet, the WebAuthn/passkeys context will no longer be filled from this code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernamePasswordForm.java:161 — During re-authentication passkeys are offered regardless of whether the user actually has a passwordless credential configured (no credentialManager check).

adjudication.rationale: In `UsernamePasswordForm`, passkeys UI setup is now triggered whenever `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` is true (i.e., `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`). There is no check that the identified user actually has a passwordless WebAuthn credential configured before calling `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` (both in `authenticate()` and in `challenge(...)`). This means during re-authentication (where `context.getUser()` is typically non-null), passkeys can be offered solely based on realm/feature enablement, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/webauthn/passwordless/PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:338 — No test covers re-authentication where the passkey belongs to a different user (WEBAUTHN_ERROR_DIFFERENT_USER path), which is the main security edge case now reachable because passkeys are offered while a user is already set.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes UsernamePasswordForm to set up conditional passkeys when a user is already known (`isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` returns true only when `user != null`), whereas previously WebAuthn context setup was only done when `context.getUser() == null`. This makes WebAuthn/passkeys UI and flow reachable during re-authentication (user already set). The added tests in `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest` cover re-authentication success paths and an incorrect-password case, but nothing in the diff exercises the security-relevant scenario of attempting WebAuthn with a credential belonging to a different user (the referenced `WEBAUTHN_ERROR_DIFFERENT_USER`-type edge case). This is a specific, diff-grounded missing-test concern rather than a proven functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.java:53 — The new setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError call on a passkey error has no test that fails a passkey during re-auth and asserts the username stays hidden and registration disabled.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context);` to the passkey error path in `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator#createErrorResponse(...)`, which conditionally sets `LoginFormsProvider.USERNAME_HIDDEN` and `REGISTRATION_DISABLED` when the re-authentication auth note (`USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH`) is true. The added/updated tests cover re-authentication with passkeys and password failures, but none exercise a *failed passkey attempt during re-authentication* and then assert that the username remains hidden and registration stays disabled on the subsequent error page. That is a specific, diff-grounded missing-test concern for newly introduced logic rather than a proven functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/webauthn/passwordless/PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:279 — reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey turns passkeys off at the realm level, so it never checks the case its name describes (a user with no passkey while realm passkeys are enabled).

adjudication.rationale: In `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey`, the realm is explicitly configured with `setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)` and the assertions expect no `//form[@id='webauth']` both on initial login and during `prompt=login` re-auth. That means this test does not exercise the scenario suggested by the finding (or by the method name) where realm passkeys are enabled but the current user has no passkey; it only covers “realm passkeys disabled”. This is a test naming/coverage mismatch, not a product bug shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/webauthn/passwordless/PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:376 — The comment says "password of different user" but the test only checks an invalid password, not a cross-user credential, so the comment overstates what is covered.

adjudication.rationale: In the re-authentication test, the code explicitly uses `loginPage.login(getPassword("test-user@localhost"));` while the authenticated user under test is `USERNAME` ("userwebauthn"). That is indeed the password for a different user being supplied as the current user’s password, so the comment "password of different user" matches what the test does.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/webauthn/passwordless/PasskeysUsernameFormTest.java:261 — The UsernameForm and organization re-auth tests only assert the final appPage after automatic passkey login, never that the re-auth form was shown with passkeys, so a regression that silently skips re-auth would still pass.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added re-authentication tests in `PasskeysUsernameFormTest` and `PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest`, after calling `oauth.loginForm().prompt(OIDCLoginProtocol.PROMPT_VALUE_LOGIN).open()` the code immediately asserts `appPage.assertCurrent()` and validates a second `events.expectLogin()` without ever asserting that a re-authentication/login UI was actually presented (e.g., `loginPage.assertCurrent()`, info message, or presence of the WebAuthn/passkeys form). This means a change that bypasses/auto-satisfies re-authentication (never showing the re-auth form with passkeys) could still satisfy these assertions if it results in a login redirect and event, unlike the more explicit checks added in `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest` (which asserts the re-auth page and WebAuthn form).
